reason: Only a new incoming friend conversation requires admission. Its first approval persists across requests, completion, cancellation and restart. Owner input never requires friend admission, including in a conversation still awaiting its first decision. Existing owner conversations use their own permissions. The grant seeds the conversation's first ordinary permission policy and initial writable roots; later requests preserve that policy and location. Replies bind the original device/request/conversation.

conversationAdmission._why: A request's running state is not permission to use its conversation. Reviewing each request blocked the owner after the previous request ended and made a persistent chat repeatedly ask for approval.

approvalStartup._why: The owner has already received the request. Approving it must start the ordinary running UI and work clock before asynchronous preparation, without resending its visible message. Local acknowledgement must not wait for cloud receiver discovery; execution still validates transport and friendship before model admission.

resourceModesWhy: The legacy grant mode seeds only the first permission policy for the task conversation. The conversation's own saved policy is authoritative afterward, so grant or global-default changes never overwrite a selection the owner made in the conversation.

shellExecution._why: Friend conversations use the ordinary runtime policy instead of a task resource scope. The grant only seeds the first policy and adds initial writable roots. Default and automatic-review keep workspace-write; full access is the ordinary danger-full-access policy.

friendInboxDiscovery._why: Notifications are transient. A parked request must remain discoverable in the friend's sidebar group without clicking one, including after a reload or a change received during an earlier snapshot read.

pendingTaskNotice._why: A task that waits for the owner's authorization must reach the owner even when Klaus is unfocused, and clicking that banner must land on the one approval it is about. The click target rides in the notification group because a delivered banner is restored from Notification Center with only its group preserved, so it has to distinguish a friend task from a conversation-shaped id.

autoArrivalNotice._why: An automatic admission asks the owner for nothing, so without an arrival notice the task would run invisibly until someone opened the sidebar. It rides the friend-message arrival tiers instead of the pending-task banner: silent while the task conversation is open, in-app toast while a window is focused, desktop banner while unfocused.

globalBypassExpandsScopeWhy: Full access is the same danger-full-access preset as an ordinary conversation, so it is not narrowed by the friend grant's directories. The grant's application selection and task-admission identity remain independent.
allowPrivateContextAutoloadWhy: A friend conversation uses the ordinary host context and tool loading path; the friend's message remains untrusted and is never permission authority.
localLifecycleWhy: Approval is persistent within one conversation and never transfers to another conversation or friendship. Request completion and restart retain it. Host-authored terminal notices keep local status metadata, and ignored requests have no elapsed-time expiry.

asyncInteraction._why: Display messages remain unread until seen without running a model. Explicit local assistance opens a local chat whose first turn is the friend's message itself, recorded with the friend's sender attribution instead of the owner's prompt. Request progress updates the original bubble; all originally targeted device results contribute to a single asynchronous continuation that requires an explicit unresolved consuming task, rechecks its identity and original input, and gives owner updates priority.

continuationIdentity._why: Saved input and reply associations use the engine turn ID; mid-turn admission uses the distinct facade submission ID. Comparing the submission ID with saved history rejects a valid request before sending it.

friendLocalAssistWhy: Explicit recipients send the original text with a visible purpose selector; legacy local-assistance settings cannot start local inference.

friendContext._why: Every friend row a conversation shows also reaches the model, the open session and a resumed one alike, tagged with who sent it, what it is for and what it answers; the transcript keeps the plain words. Each turn of a conversation with friend traffic carries the friend rules and the collaborations still open. Klaus sends no interim progress, and whether a friend message needs the owner's approval follows the conversation's permission mode, with no separate draft confirmation.

friendNoticeSidebarGrouping._why: Display-only conversations belong to their sender's friendship without acquiring a task grant. Existing unlinked notice conversations recover their group from the first durable display record; replies routed into an owner's existing conversation retain that conversation's group.

friendGroupThreadTitle._why: The folder already identifies the friend, so its conversations hide the recorded sender prefix without changing stored titles or titles outside the folder. The recorded name also works when the owner uses a different remark or the friend changes their nickname.
